## Section 2: Borrower Overview and Relationship History

### 2.1 Borrower Overview

Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. ("Larkspur") is privately held. [D5, ¶1] It was founded in 1994 in Rockford, Illinois, by Erik and Maria Halvorsen. [D5, ¶1]

Larkspur makes precision-machined components and welded assemblies for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs. [D5, ¶1] It has about 310 employees and one plant. [D5, ¶1]

Ownership: Erik Halvorsen 55%, Maria Halvorsen 25%, and Anders Halvorsen (COO) 20%. [D5, ¶1] The draft credit agreement defines "Founders" as Erik Halvorsen and Maria Halvorsen. [D2, §1.1]

Customer A accounted for 28% of FY2024 revenue and 31% of FY2025 revenue. [D1, §5] The top five customers accounted for 64% of FY2025 revenue. [D1, §5] Management commentary states that FY2025 revenue growth came from new agricultural OEM programs. [D1, §6]

Fiscal year ends December 31. [D1, header] FY2023-FY2025 financial statements were audited by Hartwell & Lo LLP, with unqualified opinions. [D1, header]

### 2.2 Relationship History

Larkspur has been a Meridian deposit and treasury management customer since 2019. [D5, ¶2] Average operating deposits were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026. [D5, ¶2]

A $12.0 million facility ($7.0M term loan, $5.0M revolver) was approved in June 2023. [D5, ¶2] The relationship notes state it has been paid as agreed with no past dues. [D5, ¶2] The prior memo described the June 2023 request as a new senior secured facility to refinance existing bank debt and fund working capital. [D3, Part B, §1]

At FY2025, Meridian exposure was a term loan of 5,600 and a revolver of 3,200. [D1, §4]

Under the existing 2023 credit agreement, the FY2025 compliance certificate is dated April 28, 2026. [D1, §7] It reports compliance with both financial covenants. [D1, §7]

On 2025-03-14, the relationship notes record that the Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late. [D5, ¶3] Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant (waiver W-25-0117). [D5, ¶3] All later certificates arrived on time. [D5, ¶3]

### 2.3 Current Request and Ownership and Management Developments

On the 2026-08-19 call, Erik and Anders Halvorsen asked to increase the facility to $18.0 million. [D5, ¶4] The purpose is to fund a 60,000 sq ft expansion of the Rockford plant ($6.0 million), tied to a new multi-year Customer A program. [D5, ¶4] They want to close by November 30, 2026 so construction can start before winter. [D5, ¶4] They said a national bank has offered a term sheet within 10 business days. [D5, ¶4]

Management expects the plant expansion to add Customer A program capacity beginning in 2027. [D1, §6]

On the 2026-09-02 call, Erik Halvorsen (64) said he plans to hand the CEO role to Anders within three years. [D5, ¶5] The family has informally discussed selling a minority stake to a private equity firm. [D5, ¶5] There is no timeline and no LOI. [D5, ¶5]

The draft agreement makes it an Event of Default if the Founders cease to own "a meaningful portion of the voting equity interests of the Borrower, or cease to be actively involved in the management of the Borrower." [D2, §7.6] "Meaningful portion" and "actively involved" are not defined in the excerpt. Flagged for the underwriter and legal. This draft does not interpret them.

**Sources used:** D1 (header, §4, §5, §6, §7); D2 (§1.1, §7.6); D3 (Part B, §1); D5 (¶1, ¶2, ¶3, ¶4, ¶5).

**Underwriter to complete:**
- Header fields: Borrower, Request type, Total commitment, Underwriter, Senior reviewer, Date.
- Not in provided documents: the current CEO and other officer titles beyond Anders Halvorsen as COO [D5, ¶1]. D5 notes a planned CEO handover but does not name the current CEO. Company records would normally hold this.
- Not in provided documents: the company's market position, competitors and industry conditions. The bank's licensed industry research feed would normally hold these.
- Not in provided documents: customer names or the contract terms of the Customer A program. Customer contracts or borrower diligence materials would normally hold these.
- Not in provided documents: the terms of waiver W-25-0117 beyond "the reporting covenant" [D5, ¶3], and which specific covenant section it addressed. Credit Administration's waiver record would normally hold these.
- Legal and underwriter review: the undefined terms "meaningful portion" and "actively involved" in D2 §7.6, given the planned CEO transition and informal minority-stake discussion [D5, ¶5]. Anders Halvorsen is not within the D2 "Founders" definition [D2, §1.1].
- Policy: D4 §4.2.4 requires customer concentration to be addressed in Section 7 if a single customer exceeds 25% of revenue in the most recent fiscal year. Section 7 is underwriter-authored. The cited facts are D1 §5: Customer A at 31% of FY2025 revenue and the top five customers at 64%.
